newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senator urges Swiss accounting of Nazi deposits.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senator urges Swiss accounting of Nazi deposits.

text.p: A senior U.S. senator on Tuesday accused Switzerland of 50 years of deception over the amount of funds deposited in Swiss banks by the Nazis during the Second World War.

Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, a New York Republican, urged U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher to seek a full accounting from Switzerland of any assets from European Jews and others taken by the Nazis.

"We must obtain the truth after 50 years of deception and manipulation by the Swiss. Our research clearly shows that the Swiss have much for which to make amends," D'Amato said in a letter to Christopher. D'Amato chairs the Senate Banking Committee, which has been investigating the issue.

"I must state honestly that the volume of documents that my staff has found both in the National Archives, as well as the archives of other nations, suggests that Switzerland has not been honest with the United States or our allies.

"Swiss banks clearly collaborated with the Nazis, taking in vast amounts of gold, securities and other movable property in safety deposit boxes, that ultimately were taken from the victims of Nazi aggression," he said.
The National Archives is the official U.S. storehouse of government records.

The Swiss government last week promised to pay more than $800,000 to two Holocaust groups in a gesture sought by Jewish groups after Switzerland apologised last year for turning back refugees from Nazi terror.

The Swiss cabinet last week also approved a decree to set up a historical commission to examine the fate of assets left in Switzerland by Nazis and their victims, parallel to a panel of Swiss and Jewish experts agreed by Swiss banks in May to search for lost Holocaust accounts.
